New home sales rise in October despite affordability challenges
November 25, 2026 | 9:58 am CST
New home sales rise in October despite affordability challenges
WASHINGTON, D.C. — New home sales unexpectedly rose to a yearly high in October, even as buyers face high mortgage rates, affordability challenges and economic uncertainty.

Sales of newly built single-family homes rose 14.2% in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 701,000, following a downward revision to the September numbers, according to new data from the U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. October sales were 7.5% above a year earlier, while year-to-date sales are down 3%.
The median new home sales price in October remained steady, down 0.3% from September to $391,300 and was down 3.2% from a year ago.

“New home sales increased in October, but the overall pace of sales remains constrained by affordability challenges,” said Bill Owens, chairman of the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB) and home builder and remodeler from Worthington, Ohio. “Builders are responding with incentives and pricing adjustments, but a more sustained improvement in affordability will be important for strengthening housing demand.”

“While the modest increase in sales is encouraging, it is too early to interpret the gain as a sustained recovery in housing demand,” said Danushka Nanayakkara-Skillington, NAHB assistant vice president for forecasting and analysis. “Elevated mortgage rates and high home prices continue to limit purchasing power, and the outlook for new home sales remains sensitive to financing costs and broader economic conditions.”

A new home sale occurs when a sales contract is signed, or a deposit is accepted. The home can be in any stage of construction: not yet started, under construction or completed. In addition to adjusting for seasonal effects, the October reading of 701,000 units is the number of homes that would sell if this pace continued for the next 12 months.

New single-family home inventory in October fell to 470,000 units, down 1.5% from September, and down 4.1% compared to a year ago. This represents an elevated 8.0 months’ supply at the current building pace. Completed, ready-to-occupy inventory consisted of 114,000 homes in October. The combined months’ supply of both new and resale homes is 5.4 months at the current building pace.
Regionally, on a year-to-date basis, new home sales were down 8.3% in the Northeast, 1.8% in the Midwest, and 11.1% in the West. New home sales were up 0.1% in the South.
